summary: Rewrite our CLI for faster startup? Measured ceiling is about 6% of machine CPU during a drain (AISDLC-1441)

options.description: no rewrite; file a task to cut node CLI startup in the current stack (lazy subcommand imports, compile cache) and remeasure (recommended)
run the 24 h sample during a normal drain first and attach its report before deciding
fund a rewrite spike of one hot CLI in a compiled language, accepting a ceiling of about 6% machine CPU and no GitHub latency gain

body:
taskId: AISDLC-1441
sourceWorktree: /Users/dominique/Documents/dev/ai-sdlc/ai-sdlc/.worktrees/aisdlc-1441

Measurement report: docs/operations/process-load-measurement-2026-11.md (AISDLC-1441 PR). Startup benchmarks (median of 20, operator machine): compiled no-op 1 ms CPU, node -e 0 26 ms, node pipeline-cli CLI --help 299 ms, gh --version 52 ms (95 ms through the logging shim), git 10 ms. 24 h exact gh log: 27,856 calls (1,161/h), 0.14-0.26% of machine CPU capacity; a real gh API call is 506 ms wall of which 44 ms is gh startup. 29.5 min sampled window: our tooling 27% of machine CPU; ceiling for a faster-starting CLI about 5.7% of machine CPU (0.27 core), of which about 4.6% is our own module loading (reachable in node via lazy imports or compile cache) and 0.5% the node runtime. Not removable by a rewrite: GitHub latency and server-side limits, work inside the CLIs (about 80% of their CPU), git, model sessions, other desktop load. The full 24 h ps sample has not been run yet (command in the report).
